description:
Measure what a mutation's whole-log read costs at scale, and determine whether the single-pass capture specification can take the event log as length and tail instead of whole bytes.

## Background

Epic criterion REQ-02 requires a label update's median wall time on a repository whose event log is ten times larger to differ by less than 10 % from the same update on the original repository.

Two whole-log costs sit on the mutation path today. The finalizer copies the whole log and recomposes it (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:1224`), which `b4483ad6` replaces with a positioned append. Capture also reads the log whole into the image, and `c88822a5` REQ-03 keeps it there: "The capture's base specification reads the registries, the index, the event log, the indexed issue files, and the plan documents a transition rule consults."

Once the append encoding lands, the read is what remains. The pre-commit conflict check already compares the log as its length plus its last `min(len, 4096)` bytes (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs`, `faa668c9`), not as whole bytes. The whole-log *parse* is claim-specific (`captured_events`, `mutation.rs:695`, reached only from the `ClaimIssue` arm at `:884`).

This issue answers, with measurements rather than argument, whether REQ-02 is reachable while capture reads the log whole.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed measurement reports the cost of reading the event log into the capture image at the benchmark fixture's 1x and 10x sizes, separated from the rest of a label update.
- [hard] REQ-02: The measurement states the projected 10x-versus-1x difference for a label update once the positioned append removes the whole-log rewrite, and whether that difference is under 10 %.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every consumer of the captured event-log bytes is enumerated with its `file:line`, and each is classified as needing the whole log, a bounded tail, or only length.
- [hard] REQ-04: The finding states whether `c88822a5` REQ-03 can stand as written, and if it cannot, states the amendment it needs and which consumers block it.
- [hard] REQ-05: No production behaviour changes in this issue.

## Notes

Investigation only. It exists because `c88822a5` lands at wave 16 and the epic's REQ-02 evidence is produced at wave 21; discovering there that the criterion is unreachable would put remediation on top of finished work.

Not redo-record delivery; excluded from the redo-record subtotal of the epic's REQ-06 line balance (`ER-01`).
title: Whole-log read cost and the single-pass capture specification
